sources.title: Structured tagged three-day peak/valley SQL question
SQLite Date And Time Functions documentation

claims.text: The source preserves only the sparse three-day peak/valley prompt; schema, dialect, strictness, and result grain are explicitly treated as assumptions.
LAG brings the previous two ordered rows into the current row, while explicit Julian-day differences prove calendar-day adjacency in the SQLite fixture.
The exact SQL detects strict rising/falling three-day windows, rejects equal-value and missing-day sequences, and emits overlapping windows for longer monotonic runs.

validation.command: extract exact candidate SQL; deterministic SQLite fixture plus 500 independently generated sparse/equal/random daily-series datasets checked against a Python oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS deterministic=1 randomized=500 strict_up_down=pass equality_break=pass missing_day_break=pass four_day_rise_two_windows=pass oracle_match=pass
checks: four-day rise produces overlapping three-day windows

findings: The candidate keeps the sparse repository source boundary explicit instead of inventing a real schema or pretending the phrase “波峰波谷，连续三天” uniquely defines output granularity.
It chooses a clear, executable three-calendar-day sliding-window contract and explicitly distinguishes strict monotonic rise/fall from a different local peak/valley interpretation.
The SQL checks date adjacency as well as row adjacency, preventing a missing calendar day from being misclassified as a continuous three-day trend.
Strict comparison semantics, one-row-per-day input grain, NULL handling boundary, overlapping windows in a four-day run, and dialect differences are all surfaced.
The exact SQL agrees with an independent oracle across the deterministic boundary fixture and 500 randomized sparse/equal-valued datasets.
The answer correctly identifies LAG as the mechanism for projecting the previous two ordered rows and limits julianday to the executable SQLite fixture rather than claiming it is portable SQL.
The project section remains hypothetical and contains no fabricated production metrics or experience.
